market_view: Calm bull regime with positive momentum broadly across equities and commodities. The primary regime signal is constructive, but the alternatives agent reading 'stressed' suggests underlying cross-asset tension — possibly commodity supply disruption or credit stress not fully reflected in equity prices. We position for continued upside while maintaining meaningful commodity and defensive allocations as portfolio insurance.
regime_assessment: HMM regime: calm_bull. This is a risk-on environment historically, but the divergence between the main regime (calm_bull) and the alternatives agent (stressed) warrants caution. We allocate ~65% to equities and ~35% to commodities/alternatives/cash as a hedge against regime transition. No past verdicts or calibration data available for this regime, so we rely on quant agent consensus and momentum signals.
quant_baseline_summary: US Equities agent: 10 equal-weight names with diverse sector exposure (CBOE, CHRD, EWY, HUM, SATS, SNDK, STRL, VICR, VRT, WDC). Macro agent: heavy commodities (PDBC 30%, DBB 30%, KMLM 30%) with light USD. International agent: Asia-heavy (EWY, EWT, EEM) plus Canada. Alternatives agent: defensive with commodities (PDBC, DBA) and T-bills (BIL). All skill scores unavailable.

key_risks: Momentum concentration: Several positions have extreme 252-day returns (SATS, VICR, STRL, WDC). Even after trimming, a broad momentum reversal could cause significant drawdowns.
EM/Asia concentration: ~20% in EWY/EWT/EEM exposes the portfolio to geopolitical risk (China-Taiwan tensions, Korean Peninsula) and USD strength.

Regime transition risk: The alternatives agent reading 'stressed' while the main regime reads 'calm_bull' may be an early warning of regime change. Our 35% non-equity allocation mitigates but doesn't fully hedge this.
Signal data gap: SEC filings, earnings transcripts, and narrative shift signals were all unavailable. We are operating purely on momentum and quant agent signals without fundamental confirmation.
Commodity correlation: PDBC + DBB + DBA + CHRD + EWC all have commodity sensitivity. In a demand destruction scenario, these would correlate to the downside.
what_could_be_wrong: The biggest risk to this portfolio is that we are late-cycle in a momentum-driven rally and the alternatives agent's 'stressed' signal is the correct forward-looking read. If we are on the cusp of a regime transition from calm_bull to stressed/crisis, our equity momentum positions could see sharp reversals while our 35% defensive allocation may not provide sufficient offset. Additionally, without any fundamental signal confirmation (all SEC/earnings/narrative caches empty), we are essentially running a pure momentum + quant agent consensus strategy — which works well in calm_bull but can be catastrophic at turning points. The SNDK exclusion could also be wrong if the +3467% return reflects a genuine fundamental re-rating we're missing.
